failure_modes: He never sees it: every mechanism needs a Pyrelands home map, a live burn-line and fire clock, a present non-hostile Tribes faction, and then a roll (rite fraction, storyteller chance, min fires); nothing has ever been run live end to end, so in real play it may simply never fire and nothing says why.

It reads wrong when it fires: the visit party walks to the fire and leaves without harvesting (a pointless visitor, not a farmer), harvesters path through the flames or burn, or a rite party ends in a fight; the Tribes then look like victims or tourists instead of the fire's farmers.

The punishment feels arbitrary: arson debt grows invisibly from any colony-owned fire, his tamed fire-hawk and furnace-beast included, and a raid lands with no warning he could act on; or the franchise split breaks quietly (thornvine left in the wrong tier) so a neighbour's mechanic fails on a load without this mod.

root.text: The Deep Desert Tribes are the Pyrelands' fire harvesters. They come into the Pyrelands now and then for their fire rite and to reap what the fire leaves, then go home to the deep desert; the Pyre burns with or without them. On a Pyrelands map, some of the fire's scheduled burns arrive with people: a small Tribes party walks in off the sand and the line catches where they stand; they work the black behind the front picking scorch-fruit without stepping into the flames, and leave carrying what they took. When a lot of fire is already standing, a peaceful Tribes group may also walk in to the burn. If your colonists pick scorch-fruit during one of their events, the Tribes warn them, then attack to drive them away: a defence of the fruit, not a full-blown raid. The Tribes keep no count of your colony's fires (they cannot see you all the time), and they never blame you for anything an animal does. Attack them openly and they raid you back, and they may go on raiding you later. Judged first: a rite party seen in ordinary play, lighting the grass, picking scorch-fruit in the scar behind the front, and walking off the map with it.

Actually just remove the count thing... that's a mechanic we don't even need. They can't see you all the time. And never do they react to an animal doing something to blame the player. Attacking them overtly makes them raid you back of course, and they may continue to do so later.
